Subject: Inference ops roadmap and next asks — CatalystRx

Alex — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same checklist.

High-level goals we captured:
- Reduce user-facing latency for interactive inference (chat) while keeping unit cost < $0.002/token for 99% of daytime traffic.
- Support peak synchronous traffic up to ~200 concurrent interactive sessions, bursting to ~350 for short windows.
- Keep QA / PHI-sensitive inference within VPC/on-prem (CatalystRx requirement).

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Current vendor has 95th p latency spikes up to ~1.2s on 512-token outputs during peak.
- Throughput cliffs when models hit kv-cache misses; prefix-heavy workload (many repeated system prompts).
- Procurement and security review (SOC2 artifacts + evidence) required by 11/12.

Technical targets we discussed (initial alignment):
- Latency SLO: p95 generation end-to-end <= 400ms for 512-token median workload, p99 <= 800ms during normal peaks.
- Baseline throughput: 120 sustained RPS with 2.5s average generation time; burst to 350 RPS for short durations (1–5 min).
- Model baseline: 13B-class chat model (open family), quantized to int8/4 for production. Evaluate 7B distilled variant for low-latency paths.

Immediate next steps / owners:
- Jordan: run a quick internal cost/throughput estimate and propose an initial topology by EOD 10/25.
- Marissa: prepare a short benchmark plan and sample runbook (include kv-cache config and batching options). Target 10/27 for sample numbers.
- Alex: share security questionnaire and any network constraints (VPC subnets, allowed egress) by 10/26.

Attachments: placeholder security questionnaire reference you mentioned — please send actual PDF if different.

Thanks — Jordan Blake

Jordan / team — notes from the technical side after digesting the call and Alex's payload numbers. Keeping this terse so we can convert directly into a bench plan.

Recommended starting topology (proof-of-concept):
- Private VPC deployment (customer-managed) with Redwood control-plane integration.
- Model variants served behind smart router: primary = 13B quantized (int8), fallback = 7B distilled quantized.
- Serving nodes: mix of 2x A100 40GB per model replica (for throughput) + 1x H100 80GB for burst/low-latency paths. Use pod-level autoscaling by queue length and token throughput.
- KV/cache strategy: persistent prefix cache in front of model replicas + per-replica KV cache for recent tokens. Target cache hit rate >= 65% to hit latency targets.
- Batching: adaptive batching with 20–50ms hold window; prefer continuous batching with latency SLO ceilings so p95 stays < 400ms.

Performance estimate (rough, to validate in bench):
- 13B quantized on A100: ~450 tokens/sec per GPU when generating; with 2 GPUs per replica => ~900 tokens/sec.
- 7B quantized variant: ~1300 tokens/sec per 40GB GPU.
- If avg response is 180 tokens, one 13B replica (2 GPUs) can serve ~5 RPS sustained; scale replicas to meet target RPS.

Bench plan (deliverables):
- Marissa: run synthetic replay using your sample traces (please provide) for 10/27. Capture p50/p95/p99 latencies and token/sec per replica.
- Ben: produce a low-level cost projection (on-host and egress) and a model variant cost delta for quant/7B fallback by 10/26.

I'll prepare a diagram of the proposed VPC topology and autoscaler triggers and drop it in the shared folder by 10/26.
